_readme: DAILY ENGLISH - the rotating tip shown by the 'tip' block.
One item is picked per day from the whole list, by date, so every visitor
sees the same one on the same day and it changes without a rebuild. The
build also writes one item into the page as ordinary HTML, so a reader with
no JavaScript still sees a real tip rather than an empty box.
WHY THIS IS NOT A POP-UP: it sits in the page where a reader naturally
pauses. It interrupts nothing, blocks nothing, and needs no dismissing.
A timed pop-up would be a content-blocking interstitial, which Google
treats as a mobile usability fault, and which would be a poor idea while
the site is under AdSense review.
KINDS
quote     A short quotation. Attribution must be certain - see below.
grammar   One point, stated plainly, with an example.
teaching  Something a teacher can use in the next lesson.
exam      IELTS, PTE or O/L technique.
QUOTATIONS: only well-attested ones. A great many language quotations
circulate with the wrong name attached - 'to have another language is to
possess a second soul' is not Charlemagne's, and 'tell me and I forget' is
not Franklin's. If the source cannot be named with confidence, leave it out.
Keep each quotation short.
FIELDS
kind    quote | grammar | teaching | exam
text    The tip itself. One or two sentences.
source  For a quotation, who said or wrote it. Empty otherwise.
note    Optional second line - an example, or what to do with it.

tips.text: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head. If you talk to him in his language, that goes to his heart.
Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.
Language is the dress of thought.
tips.source: Samuel Johnson, Lives of the Poets

tips.text: Grammar is the logic of speech, even as logic is the grammar of reason.
tips.source: Richard Chenevix Trench, On the Study of Words

tips.text: The beautiful thing about learning is that no one can take it away from you.
A word after a word after a word is power.
Words are, of course, the most powerful drug used by mankind.
Use the present perfect when the time is not finished or not stated: I have taught here for ten years. Use the past simple when the time is over: I taught there in 2019.
tips.note: If the sentence names a finished time, the present perfect is wrong.

tips.text: Since marks a point in time; for marks a length of time. Since 2019, for six years.
Few and a few are not the same. A few friends came means some came. Few friends came means almost nobody did.
tips.note: The same holds for little and a little.

tips.text: Each and every take a singular verb: Every student has a book, not have.
Used to describes a past habit that has stopped: I used to walk to school. Be used to means accustomed, and takes -ing: I am used to walking.
tips.note: Two different structures that look alike. Teach them apart, not together.

tips.text: In reported speech, say takes no person: She said that she was tired. Tell needs one: She told me that she was tired.
The passive is not a way of being polite. Use it when the doer is unknown, obvious, or not the point: The road was widened last year.
tips.note: If the doer matters, the active is clearer.

tips.text: Its is the possessive; it's is it is or it has. The apostrophe never makes a possessive pronoun.
tips.note: Nor do hers, theirs or yours take one.

tips.text: Adjective order in English is fixed and nobody is taught it: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material. A lovely little old round brown Sri Lankan wooden box.
tips.note: Learners get this wrong and cannot say why. Give them the order.

tips.text: Neither and either take a singular verb when both items are singular: Neither answer is correct.
The second conditional uses the past form for an unreal present: If I had the money, I would buy it. The past form here is not past time.
tips.note: Were is correct for all persons: If I were you.

tips.text: Some words are uncountable in English although they are countable in Sinhala and Tamil: information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment. Not informations.
tips.note: Use a piece of information, two items of furniture.

tips.text: Ask the question before you name the pupil. Name first and the rest of the class stops listening.
Wait three seconds after asking a question. Most teachers wait less than one, and the pupils who need longest never answer at all.
tips.note: Count it silently. Three seconds is longer than it feels.

tips.text: Correct the error, not the child. Repeat the sentence correctly and move on; a pupil corrected in front of forty others stops volunteering.
In a class of forty, pair work gives every pupil twenty minutes of speaking in a forty-minute lesson. Whole-class questioning gives most of them none.
Write the lesson's one new structure on the board before you begin, and leave it there. A pupil who loses the thread can find it again without asking.
A game is worth the period only if it produces more language per pupil than the alternative. Judge it by that, not by how lively the room is.
Set the task before handing out the paper. Once a pupil has the sheet, they are reading it and not listening to you.
Give the weakest reader the sentence you know they can manage. Success is what makes a child read again; difficulty is what stops them.
In IELTS Writing Task 2, plan for two minutes before you write. Forty minutes is enough for a planned essay and not enough for an unplanned one.
In IELTS Writing Task 1, do not explain why the figures changed. You are asked to report what the data shows, and guessing at causes earns nothing.
In PTE Summarize Written Text the answer must be one sentence. Two sentences score zero for form however good the content is.
tips.note: Join with although, while or because rather than starting again.

tips.text: PTE is marked by machine, so hesitation costs more than a plain word choice. Say the ordinary word and keep going.
In the O/L paper, answer the question that was asked. A good essay on a slightly different question earns the marks of a weak essay on the right one.
Read the instruction for the word limit and obey it. Examiners stop reading where the limit ends, and the best sentence after it is not read.
In a listening test, read the questions before the recording starts. You cannot listen for an answer you have not yet seen.
Leave nothing blank in a multiple-choice paper where wrong answers cost nothing. An unanswered question is certainly wrong; a guess sometimes is not.
tips.note: Check the rule first: PTE's multiple-answer questions do penalise wrong choices.
